title: RF mesh AODV/root-aware design and implementation plan
goal: Design and later implement a pragmatic project-owned RF mesh path for micro:bit v2/nRF52833 using proprietary 2.4 GHz radio semantics, with root-aware/AODV-style discovery, bounded flood/relay behavior, dummy payloads, and strict no-hardware/no-flash gates during planning and software validation.
scope: Workflow planning and later staged implementation for the RF mesh lane in `/home/lucas/Workspace/tron-worktrees/rf-mesh`.
Use current codebase reality: C/CMake μT-Kernel firmware under `microbit/`, existing BLE beacon/observer examples only, no RF mesh implementation yet.
Project-owned RF packet/routing design unless the user later overrides with an explicit compatibility requirement.
Implementation-facing protocol/radio ABI design before parallel code work.
Hardware-independent packet/routing/dedup/backoff core with non-hardware validation.
New proprietary RF radio driver and `rf_mesh_node` firmware target.
Code-checker gates before any hardware-related follow-up.
nonGoals: No MakeCode/MicroPython wire compatibility unless the user later overrides this plan.
No ESP32 sidecar RF work in this lane.
No final application payload semantics; payloads remain dummy/test-only for now.
No hardware flashing, no pyOCD/probe/reset/erase/load commands, and no hardware runtime claims in this planning/software-validation workflow.
No dependency upgrades or submodule pointer advances.
constraints: No hardware actions, no flash commands, no pyOCD probe/list/reset/erase/load, and no `flash.sh` during this workflow.

Any future flash/run step requires a separate approved hardware plan, code-checker hardware-safety review, Hermes approval, probe UID targeting, and replacement/avoidance of the current mass-erase behavior unless explicitly approved.
One radio only: no true simultaneous TX/RX; all mesh behavior must be scheduled/interleaved.
Treat the approved conceptual schema as authoritative for now because no concrete local schema/spec file is visible; do not continue schema hunting unless the user reopens that question.
Initialize the existing `microbit/libs/mtkernel_3` submodule only to the repo-pinned commit; do not advance the submodule pointer or vendor new dependency contents.
Keep changes small and staged; freeze interfaces before safe parallel code-writer tasks.
Protocol details may evolve after later user comments; v1 must be sane, bounded, and testable rather than final.
Payloads remain dummy/test-only until an application payload spec is approved.

steps.title: Record schema authority and stop schema hunting
steps.action: Carry forward the prior finding that no concrete local schema/spec/protocol file was visible after a narrow checkout search. Use the user-approved conceptual schema plus established research conclusions as the current authority.
steps.validation: Plan and future prompts do not reopen schema discovery unless the user explicitly asks.

steps.title: Initialize pinned μT-Kernel submodule for buildability
steps.action: Initialize the existing git submodule to the repo-pinned commit only. Do not update the submodule pointer, vendor contents, or dependency versions.
steps.validation: `git submodule status` shows the pinned commit checked out; no dependency pointer drift is present.

steps.title: Baseline build existing firmware targets only
steps.action: After the pinned submodule exists, build existing targets to establish compile baseline. Do not run flash scripts or hardware commands.
steps.validation: Build logs show success or clear software/toolchain failures; no pyOCD/hardware command was run.

steps.title: Enforce strict no-hardware boundary
steps.action: Record that this workflow performs no `flash.sh`, no pyOCD, no probe listing, no reset, no erase, no load, and no hardware runtime claims. Flag current `flash.sh` mass erase behavior as a future safety issue before any hardware plan.
steps.validation: Execution plan contains an explicit no-flash-until-code-checker-and-Hermes gate and no hardware step in scope.

phases.title: Implementation-facing protocol and radio ABI design

steps.title: Create provisional RF mesh protocol design note
steps.action: Write a concise but implementation-facing design note for v1 RF mesh. It must state that protocol details may evolve, payloads are dummy, and project-owned proprietary RF is the default.
steps.validation: Design note includes exact v1 assumptions and is sufficient for independent packet/core/radio/app work without ambiguous field ownership.

steps.title: Freeze v1 packet byte layout and field semantics
steps.action: Define exact packet byte layout, endianness, field widths, max packet size, version, message type, flags, network/root id, source id, destination/broadcast marker, sequence/request id, TTL/hop count, route metric, payload length, dummy payload bytes, and any reserved checksum/auth bytes. Specify whether checksum/auth is reserved-only or active in v1.
steps.validation: Packet ABI can be implemented and tested for valid, max-length, malformed, and truncated packets.

steps.title: Freeze nRF RADIO proprietary-mode mapping
steps.action: Define v1 radio parameters: channel/frequency, 1M/2M choice, TX power default, base/prefix/network address mapping, group/network filtering approach, RADIO packet config including S0/LENGTH/S1 use, CRC, whitening, max on-air payload, and RSSI behavior if supported.
steps.validation: RF driver implementation has concrete register-level targets without touching BLE driver behavior.

steps.title: Freeze AODV-style/root-aware routing rules
steps.action: Define message types and rules: HELLO/root beacon, RREQ, RREP, DATA with dummy payload, optional/deferred ACK. Define root configuration/election assumptions, route freshness, tie-breaking, route expiry, reverse-route handling, flood forwarding, broadcast DATA dedup, and drop behavior.
steps.validation: Core routing can be implemented deterministically and unit-tested without radio hardware.

steps.title: Freeze minimal single-radio scheduler/MAC rules
steps.action: Define RX-first state machine, max blocking TX/RX operations, jitter/backoff timing source, deterministic fallback if no randomness exists, bounded TX queue behavior, relay priority/drop policy, ACK/retry v1 decision, and guarantee BLE/RF drivers are not active in the same target.
steps.validation: App and driver work can interleave TX/RX safely without assuming simultaneous operation.

steps.title: Freeze public interfaces before parallel work
steps.target: planned headers: rf_mesh_packet.h, rf_mesh_core.h, rf_radio.h, config header/CMake defines
steps.action: Define stable function prototypes, config constants, and ownership boundaries for packet/core, radio driver, and app target. Reserve CMake integration ownership for the serial integration step to avoid parallel conflicts.
steps.validation: Parallel code-writer tasks can proceed with non-overlapping file ownership and no interface drift.

steps.title: Implement packet constants and pack/unpack helpers
steps.action: Implement v1 packet ABI from Phase 1 with explicit bounds checks, endianness helpers, and malformed/truncated packet rejection.
steps.validation: Host/non-hardware tests cover valid packets, max-length packets, malformed lengths, truncated buffers, unsupported versions/types, and dummy payload boundaries.

steps.title: Implement duplicate suppression and TTL/drop rules
steps.action: Implement bounded duplicate cache keyed by source id, sequence/request id, and message type as specified. Implement TTL decrement/drop behavior and expiry.
steps.validation: Tests cover first-seen vs duplicate, wrap behavior if specified, expiry, TTL decrement, TTL zero drop, and broadcast DATA dedup.

steps.title: Implement root-aware/AODV-style route table
steps.action: Implement fixed-size route table for destination/root id, next hop, metric/hop count, sequence freshness, last seen, expiry, tie-breaking, HELLO/RREQ/RREP update rules, and no-route behavior.
steps.validation: Tests cover route insert/update/reject, better/worse metric tie-breaks, stale route expiry, root preference, and discovery trigger decisions.

steps.title: Implement backoff scheduler and bounded TX queue policy
steps.action: Implement jitter/backoff scheduling, deterministic fallback, bounded TX queue, priority/drop rules, and counters for drops/relays/duplicates.
steps.validation: Tests cover jitter bounds, queue full policy, relay priority handling, deterministic fallback, and counter increments.

steps.title: Implement RF radio driver separate from BLE driver
steps.action: Add a new direct-register nRF52833 proprietary radio driver with `rf_radio_init`, `rf_radio_listen`, `rf_radio_poll`, `rf_radio_send`, and optional RSSI support. Do not modify `ble_radio.c/.h` except for later reviewed non-invasive shared helpers if clearly justified.
steps.validation: Driver compiles, public API matches frozen Phase 1 interface, and code review confirms no BLE mesh assumptions and no simultaneous TX/RX assumptions.

steps.title: Review radio register configuration assumptions
steps.action: Manually and with code-checker review the register configuration for mode, packet config, CRC, whitening, frequency, TX power, and state transitions. Keep operations bounded and return to RX promptly after TX.
steps.validation: Code-checker has no open critical/major findings on radio register safety, packet bounds, or state-machine assumptions before any hardware plan.

steps.title: Add rf_mesh_node app target
steps.action: Create a new firmware target using nearest existing app patterns. Include config, CMake, and main task structure. Payloads are dummy/test-only. LED/serial output is diagnostic only.
steps.validation: Target appears in CMake build graph and can compile once core/driver integration is complete.

steps.title: Define v1 node/root/network/channel configuration mechanism
steps.action: Use a concrete v1 mechanism such as compile-time config constants with optional FICR-derived node id fallback. Define root/non-root role, network id, root id, RF channel, TX power, and dummy payload interval.
steps.validation: Different node/root roles can be selected at build/config time without editing core protocol logic.

steps.title: Implement RX-first mesh event loop
steps.action: Boot radio, initialize observability, poll RX, validate/decode, update dedup/routes, enqueue relay/local dummy delivery, process bounded TX queue respecting jitter windows, then return to listen.
steps.validation: Build-only and static review confirm no full-duplex assumption, no unbounded loops beyond intended polling, and no hardware claims.

steps.title: Add serial counters and LED diagnostics
steps.action: Expose tx/rx/drop/dup/relay/route-update/current-root-metric counters over serial logs and simple LED status. Keep display diagnostic only.
steps.validation: Code review verifies counters are non-blocking enough for v1 and payload semantics remain dummy.

phases.title: Parallel slices, integration, and software validation

steps.title: Parallel code-writer Slice A: protocol core
steps.action: After Phase 1 interfaces are frozen and baseline build works, a code-writer owns packet/routing/dedup/backoff core and tests. It must not touch RF driver internals or app target CMake integration.
steps.validation: Core tests pass; code-checker reviews packet bounds, route correctness, TTL/dedup, and queue/backoff behavior.

steps.title: Parallel code-writer Slice B: RF radio driver
steps.action: After Phase 1 interfaces are frozen, a code-writer owns RF radio driver implementation. It must not touch routing core or app target logic.
steps.validation: Firmware build compiles driver when integrated; code-checker reviews register config, state transitions, and hardware safety assumptions.

steps.title: Parallel code-writer Slice C: app skeleton
steps.action: After Phase 1 interfaces are frozen, a code-writer owns app target skeleton, config, and diagnostic main loop using frozen interfaces or stubs. It must not change core internals or RF driver internals.
steps.validation: App skeleton compiles after serial integration; code-checker reviews scheduler assumptions and config clarity.

steps.title: Serial integration of core, driver, app, and CMake
steps.action: One integrator merges slices, resolves API mismatches, owns CMake source inclusion, removes stubs, and performs build-only verification.
steps.validation: Existing baseline targets still build, `rf_mesh_node` builds, and no unexpected file ownership conflicts remain.

steps.title: Run code-checker gates after each meaningful slice and final integration
steps.action: Use code-checker after Slice A, Slice B, Slice C/integration, and before any future hardware proposal. Reviews must include correctness, spec alignment, packet safety, timing assumptions, hardware safety, hard-brick risk, wrong-target/wrong-probe risk, and flash-script assumptions.
steps.validation: No unresolved critical/major findings before moving to any hardware-gated follow-up.

phases.title: Future hardware gate outside this workflow

steps.title: No flash until separate code-checker + Hermes gate
steps.action: Do not run hardware. A future flash/run phase must be separately approved, include code-checker hardware-safety review, Hermes review of exact command/target, no concurrent flashing, probe UID targeting, and explicit handling of `flash.sh` mass erase behavior.
steps.validation: This plan contains no hardware execution step and future hardware cannot proceed without explicit user/Hermes approval.

steps.title: Prepare future narrow hardware test plan only after software gates
steps.action: After all software gates pass, propose a narrow hardware test matrix: root plus one/two non-root nodes, dummy heartbeat/DATA, serial counter collection, route formation observation, and no claims beyond measured logs.
steps.validation: Future test plan remains proposal-only until Hermes approves actual commands and targets.

reviewFindings.title: Slice A dedup cache evicts unexpired entries
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved. Full unexpired dedup cache now rejects/drops new packets without evicting existing keys; tests cover this behavior. Slice A code-checker gate passes.

reviewFindings.title: Slice B RF RX single-buffer race under END_START
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved. RX now uses END_DISABLE stable handoff and restarts after rf_radio_poll handles a completed packet. Slice B code-checker gate passes.
